name: Tirisfal Glades
summary: In northern Lordaeron, Tirisfal Glades is home to Lady Sylvanas Windrunner and her Forsaken. Under blighted skies, fallen manors and dormant crypts surround their vast underground capital, the Undercity. Mindless Scourge and zealous Scarlet crusaders hem them in, and the free-willed dead fight for their survival.

sections.title: A Land in Twilight
sections.body: Tirisfal was once the fertile cradle of humanity, before the Lich King's plague withered them. The sun rarely breaks through the murky gloom over dying woods, neglected pumpkin patches and cold coastal hills. Old farmsteads like the Agamand Mills and Balnir Farmstead still stand, but most of their masters lie in mass graves or walk as restless dead. Yet a dark resilience holds on in towns like Brill and in the cloistered sanctuary of Deathknell, where freshly awakened Forsaken learn to endure their second life.

sections.title: A War on Two Fronts
sections.body: Lady Sylvanas rules the region from beneath the Ruins of Lordaeron, yet the Forsaken are beset on all sides. Scourge thralls still infest hollows, fields and crumbling crypts, wholly bound to the frozen throne of Northrend. To the east, the fanatical Scarlet Crusade has made northern Tirisfal its main bastion, centered on the Scarlet Monastery. Sworn to destroy every undead creature, its outposts and patrols wage constant guerrilla war on Forsaken scouts and civilian travelers.

sections.title: Echoes of the Ancient Past
sections.body: The story of the Glades is older than any human crown. High elven exiles once tried to settle these woods, until shadowy energies deep beneath the earth began driving them mad and they moved on north. Centuries later, the secret mortal cabal called the Council of Tirisfal chose these shadowed groves to empower its solitary Guardians, who shielded Azeroth from demons.

faq.q: Why is the sky green and the land rotting?
faq.answer: During the Third War, Prince Arthas and the Scourge unleashed the Plague of Undeath across the Kingdom of Lordaeron. The magical blight poisoned not only the populace, but the soil, trees, and water itself, leaving the glades in an eternal state of eerie, sickly decay.

faq.q: What is the difference between the Forsaken and the Scourge here?
faq.answer: The Forsaken are undead who broke free from the Lich King's telepathic domination after the Battle of Mount Hyjal, choosing to follow Lady Sylvanas Windrunner with their own free will. The Scourge roaming the farmsteads and ruins remain mindless slaves bound to the Lich King's commands.

faq.q: Who are the red-armored soldiers attacking travelers?
faq.answer: They belong to the Scarlet Crusade, an uncompromising splinter order of former Silver Hand paladins and survivors. Convinced all undead are irredeemable abominations that must be purified by sword and fire, they execute both mindless thralls and free-willed Forsaken with fanatical hatred.

faq.q: Where does the name Tirisfal come from?
faq.answer: The name is older than any human kingdom, and its true origin has been lost to history. It is best known through the Council of Tirisfal, the secret order of magi that empowered the Guardians to shield Azeroth from demons.

faq.q: Where do newly awakened Forsaken begin their journey?
faq.answer: Newly awakened Forsaken rise from the crypts of the Shadow Grave inside Deathknell, a cloistered town in southwestern Tirisfal. There, administrators and executors judge whether the risen dead have the sanity and loyalty to serve the Dark Lady.

faq.q: How do travelers leave Tirisfal for other continents?
faq.answer: A large goblin-operated zeppelin tower sits on the hillside south of Brill, right outside the Ruins of Lordaeron. These airships provide direct, regular transit across the seas to Orgrimmar in Kalimdor and Grom'gol Base Camp in Stranglethorn Vale.

angles.text: This is your ancestral homeland twice over: the kingdom you built in life, and the precarious sanctuary you must defend in undeath under Lady Sylvanas.
Tirisfal is the Horde's vital bastion in the northern Eastern Kingdoms, anchoring diplomatic ties with the Forsaken while warding off human extremists and the Scourge.
For the surviving nations of the Alliance, Tirisfal is a tragic monument to Lordaeron's fall, filled with the desecrated tombs of former brothers and sisters in faith.
Historic holy grounds like Faol's Rest—the tomb of Archbishop Alonsus Faol, founder of the Silver Hand—lie here, warped by death and contested between zealots and Shadow priests.
